q1: SELECT C.DEPT_NAME, SUM(C.CREDITS) FROM COURSE AS C INNER JOIN DEPARTMENT AS D ON (C.DEPT_NAME = D.DEPT_NAME) GROUP BY C.DEPT_NAME HAVING SUM(C.CREDITS) > 10 AND COUNT(C.CREDITS) > 5
q2: SELECT C.DEPT_NAME, SUM(C.CREDITS) FROM COURSE AS C INNER JOIN DEPARTMENT AS D ON (C.DEPT_NAME = D.DEPT_NAME) GROUP BY C.DEPT_NAME HAVING SUM(C.CREDITS) > 10 AND COUNT(C.CREDITS) > 8

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent because they have different conditions in the HAVING clause. Q1 requires COUNT(C.CREDITS) > 5, while Q2 requires COUNT(C.CREDITS) > 8. This difference can lead to different results depending on the data.
counterexample_dsp: The difference in results can be observed when the count of credits in a department is close to 10 but not exactly 10. In such cases, the department will be included in Q1 if the count is greater than 5 but will not be included in Q2 if the count is greater than 8.
